## 6. Complete budget form supplied by these substitutions
Reserve the same activity budgets and Young fractions as in the reviewed native clean proof. Before global energy density is used, the above calculations give

    (T_t^(-1)Lhat T_t)(V_sG)
       <=-a_U t epsilon^2 U V_sG
          -a_B sum_h B_h V_sG +rho_0 N V_sG,

with fixed a_U,a_B>0 (including b_min,kappa and the finite s-dependent factors), after t+delta is small enough to absorb dirty diagonals. One admissible upper source bound is

    rho_0 <= C_s[t^2+t delta+(t+delta)^2
                 +delta A0 epsilon^4
                 +t^2 epsilon^4/(delta min(A0,B0))]. (6.1)

The singleton/pair budgets absorb the other reviewed errors: t epsilon^2 M1, t M2, and t^2 epsilon^2/(delta B0) M1. All constants are actual fixed-controller/local-map constants, not assumed service rates.

Set t=c epsilon^2, delta=d epsilon^2, d=r c. Choose r sufficiently large for the activity reservations; then c small. For epsilon small,

    lambda=min(a_U c epsilon^4,a_B/R)>0,
    L_eff(V_sG)<=-lambda E V_sG+rho_0 N V_sG,
    rho_0/lambda <= C_s (c+d)^2/(c a_U)+O(epsilon^2).

Thus rho_0/lambda can be made arbitrarily small by c, then epsilon, with positive fixed parameters. The bad term is not weakened prematurely to order epsilon^4 when paying dirty errors.

Positive CP pullback T=T_B T_t gives F=T(V_sG) and

    L_native*F<=-lambda T(E V_sG)+rho_0 N F.

Physical common-bath perturbations contribute at most C_s eta N F, by local Stinespring transfer and the nonunital finite-cone relative bound. Programs, if added, remain physical local support factors. Let rho=rho_0+C_s eta. Choose eta after lambda so rho/lambda is as small as needed. This is the desired extensive-entropy-source form, rather than an O(N) additive source.
